call_overview.title: About the call
call_overview.question: What does the call offer, and who can apply?

cards.title: What the call wants
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop, and which problem or need must it address?
cards.answer:
Demonstrated industrial processes and equipment for manufacturing tandem solar cells and modules at large scale, more efficient than silicon and as durable.
Tandem PV stacks two solar-cell materials, typically perovskite on silicon, to convert more sunlight than silicon alone can. Proposals are expected to:
- demonstrate tandem technologies with lifetimes similar to silicon and efficiencies beyond the silicon limit
- demonstrate interface and thin-film engineering at large scale
- demonstrate production processes and equipment ready for large-scale deployment
The need originates with European industry and policy: the EU targets 600 GW of solar PV by 2030 and, under the Net-Zero Industry Act, European manufacturing of at least 30 GW a year, to reduce import dependence. The call also sees tandem technology as an opening for European start-ups and scale-ups.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 153–154 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-16, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: Project impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer:
Projects must contribute to all three outcomes: better commercial prospects for European tandem PV, the EU Solar PV Industry Alliance's goals, and the solar research agenda.
- Increased potential to commercialise tandem PV and competitive know-how for the European PV industrial base
- Contribution to the objectives of the EU Solar PV Industry Alliance (an industry platform to rebuild European solar manufacturing)
- Support for the solar energy joint research and innovation agenda
The wider aim is a more resilient EU PV value chain with fewer excessive dependencies, towards the 600 GW deployment and 30 GW manufacturing targets for 2030.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 153–154 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-16, Expected Outcome

cards.title: Who it suits
cards.question: Who may lead, which partners must take part, and how must the work be shared?
cards.answer:
Consortia of at least three independent organisations from three countries, typically PV manufacturers, equipment makers and research institutes; there is no prescribed lead.
- Lead: any beneficiary may coordinate; the call reserves the role for no organisation type
- Composition: the general rule requires three independent legal entities, one in an EU Member State and two others in different Member States or countries associated with Horizon Europe (non-EU countries taking part in the programme); the call names no required partner types
- Work split: none prescribed
- Exclusion: entities controlled by China or a Chinese legal entity are not eligible
The call suits PV cell and module manufacturers, production-equipment suppliers, materials companies, start-ups and scale-ups, and PV research institutes.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 153–154 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-16, Specific conditions and Expected Outcome
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 13, 36 · B — Consortium composition; IMPORTANT, Coordinator

cards.title: Innovation
cards.question: How new must the project be, and in what must it innovate?
cards.answer:
The project must demonstrate novel tandem technologies that beat silicon's efficiency limit, together with new large-scale manufacturing processes and equipment.
The innovation is in technology (cells, interfaces, thin films) and in production processes and equipment, not in system architecture or market arrangements.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 153–154 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-16, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?
cards.answer:
Activities are expected to reach TRL 6–7 by the end of the project and may start at any TRL.
TRL 6 is technology demonstrated in a relevant environment; TRL 7 is a system prototype demonstrated in an operational environment, here meaning pilot manufacturing close to industrial conditions.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 153–154 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-16, Specific conditions, Technology Readiness Level
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 15 · B — Technology Readiness Levels

cards.title: Demonstration and integration of work
cards.question: Where must the solution be demonstrated, and how must the work fit with existing systems?
cards.answer:
Demonstration of tandem devices, large-scale thin-film engineering and production processes and equipment ready for large-scale deployment, in a manufacturing setting.
The call does not prescribe a site. It asks for no integration with grids or buildings; the focus is manufacturing.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 153–154 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-16, Scope

call_overview.title: Relevance to TenneT
call_overview.question: Why is this call relevant to TenneT?

cards.title: Why it matters to TenneT
cards.question: Why does this call matter to TenneT, and why can't TenneT take part itself?
cards.answer:
More efficient PV delivers more energy per hectare and per connection, which matters for TenneT's congested grid and connection planning.
This is our interpretation. Higher module efficiency means more output from the same connection, which links to TenneT's thinking on over-planting and using connections more fully. The effect on TenneT is indirect and long-term. TenneT cannot usefully take part: the call funds PV manufacturing processes and equipment and sets out no role for a transmission system operator.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 153–154 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-16, Expected Outcome and Scope

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
About 3 projects of around EUR 9.5 million each are expected, within a topic budget of EUR 28.5 million.
- Total project size: not stated
- Grant request: around EUR 9.5 million per project, for the whole consortium; other amounts may be requested and selected
- Funding form: actual-cost grant (reimburses eligible costs actually incurred) with a 25% flat rate for indirect costs
Final budgets may change by up to 20% after evaluation.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 48–49 · Call ENERGY (HORIZON-CL5-2027-07), Overview of this call
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 153–154 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-16, Specific conditions

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
Companies such as TenneT receive at most 70% of eligible costs; non-profit legal entities receive up to 100%.
- For-profit organisations: up to 70% of eligible costs, so at least 30% must come from their own resources
- Non-profit legal entities (for example universities and research organisations): up to 100% of eligible costs
- Co-financing conditions: the call sets no rule on cash or in-kind co-financing beyond the funding rate; the remainder is simply not reimbursed
Grants may not produce a profit: any surplus of revenue plus grant over costs is deducted from the final grant.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · G — Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
The grant reimburses only eligible costs actually incurred, plus a flat 25% for indirect costs; subcontracting should stay a limited part.
- Eligible costs: personnel, subcontracting and purchase costs (equipment, travel, other goods and services), plus personnel unit costs where the beneficiary uses them
- Overheads and VAT: indirect costs are a flat rate of 25% of eligible direct costs, excluding subcontracting and financial support to third parties
- Subcontracting or equipment: subcontracting should normally be a limited part of the project and be done by third parties, not by beneficiaries; purchases must give best value for money
Budgeted costs are not paid as such: only the costs actually incurred are reimbursed.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · G — Form of grant, Budget categories and cost eligibility rules

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
One stage: full proposals are due by 1 December 2027, 17:00 Brussels time, through the EU Funding & Tenders Portal.
- Stage 1 — Full proposal: 1 December 2027, 17:00 Brussels time; Part A online and Part B of at most 40 pages
- Opening: 4 August 2027
- Additional procedure: none; the Commission may open the call up to one month earlier or later and delay the deadline by up to two months
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 48–49 · Call ENERGY (HORIZON-CL5-2027-07), Overview of this call
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 3–4 · A — Admissibility, Page limits

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
The call sets no duration or start date: both are fixed in the grant agreement.
- Maximum duration: not set by the call; the grant agreement states the duration in months, and extensions are possible only exceptionally
- Required start: normally after the grant agreement is signed; an earlier start is possible only exceptionally, for duly justified reasons and with the granting authority's agreement
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 30–31 · G — Starting date & project duration

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
Indicatively, the evaluation result comes about 5 months after the deadline and the grant agreement is signed about 8 months after it.
- Funding decision: about 5 months after the deadline (indicative), around May 2028
- Grant agreement: about 8 months after the deadline (indicative)
- Conditions before starting: an invitation to grant preparation is not yet a funding commitment, since legal entity validation, financial capacity and exclusion checks follow; the partners must sign a written consortium agreement

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
The proposal must be complete, submitted electronically before the deadline, and within the page limit; incomplete applications are rejected.
- Application form: Part A (administrative data and a summary budget, filled in online) and Part B (the technical description, uploaded as a PDF) through the EU Funding & Tenders Portal, using the forms inside the submission system; Part B is limited to 40 pages
- Budget: the summary budget in Part A
- Mandatory annexes: a plan for the exploitation and dissemination of results, including communication activities, and the ethics self-assessment
- Partner documents: the coordinator confirms at submission that it has the mandate to act for all applicants; every participant signs a declaration of honour before the grant is signed
- Registration: every beneficiary, affiliated entity and associated partner needs a participant identification code (PIC, a number from the EU Participant Register) before submission; validation of beneficiaries follows at grant preparation
- Parallel submission: none
- Exploitation plan: a strong business case and preliminary plans for scale-up, commercialisation and deployment, naming funding such as the Innovation Fund

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Independent experts score three criteria out of 5; a proposal needs 3 on each and 10 in total, and Impact weighs 1.5 times in the ranking.
- Evaluation criteria: Excellence (clear, ambitious objectives beyond the state of the art; sound methodology), Impact (credible pathways to the expected outcomes; dissemination and exploitation measures) and Quality and efficiency of the implementation (work plan, risks, resources, capacity of each partner)
- Thresholds: at least 3 out of 5 for each criterion and 10 out of 15 overall
- Weighting: for ranking, the Impact score counts 1.5 times
- Ranking rules: equal scores are separated first by whether a proposal covers aspects of the call not covered by higher-ranked ones, then by the Impact score, then Excellence, then gender balance among lead researchers and geographical diversity
- Budget assessment: the grant awarded may be lower than requested, and topic budgets may change by up to 20% after evaluation

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
The China-control restriction, the ownership safeguard, the business case and partnership reporting apply in addition to the general rules.
- Exception — entities controlled by China: not eligible
- Conditional — results transfer: the granting authority may object to transfers or exclusive licensing for 4 years after the project
- Conditional — exploitation: a strong business case and preliminary scale-up plans, naming possible funding such as the Innovation Fund
- Conditional — partnership reporting: report results to the European Partnership for Innovation in Photovoltaics (EUPI-PV)
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 153–154 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-16, Specific conditions and Scope
